=== KB-130: Troubleshoot Dropped Calls - iOS ===
# **Troubleshoot Dropped Calls - iOS**

When calls keep cutting out, the phone is usually losing its connection to the network for a moment. A weak signal, an old setting or a software glitch are the usual causes. Work through the sections below in order, and check the fix after each one.

* * *

## 

**Before you start**

Find out what the customer already tried, so you don't repeat it. If calls only drop at home and the customer uses Wi-Fi calling there, use **Troubleshoot Wi-Fi Calling** instead.

* * *

## 

**Turn Airplane mode on and off**

Open **Control Center** by swiping down from the top-right corner, tap the airplane icon, wait 10 seconds, then tap it again. This makes the phone reconnect to the network.

* * *

## 

**Restart the phone**

Press and hold the side button and either volume button until the slider appears, drag it, then turn the phone back on. Restarting clears minor glitches.

* * *

## 

**Still not working?**

If the steps above didn't help, try these next, in this order.

**Update the software**

Go to **Settings** > **General** > **Software Update** and install anything available.

**Reset network settings**

Go to **Settings** > **General** > **Transfer or Reset iPhone** > **Reset** > **Reset Network Settings**. This clears saved Wi-Fi networks and passwords, Bluetooth pairings and VPN settings, so get the customer's OK before they start.

On iPhone 8 and earlier, press and hold the top button instead of the side button to restart.

* * *

**Check the fix:** Have the customer make a test call and stay on it for two minutes. A step can look like it worked before it really has.

If none of this helps, connect the customer with a specialist. Last reviewed 2026. Written for iOS 26. Related: Turn Airplane mode on or off, Reset network settings, Back up your phone.

=== KB-136: Troubleshoot Wi-Fi Calling - iOS ===
# **Troubleshoot Wi-Fi Calling - iOS**

Wi-Fi calling lets the phone make calls over Wi-Fi where the signal is weak. When it stops working, calls at home drop or won't connect. Work through the sections below in order, and check the fix after each one.

* * *

## 

**Before you start**

Find out what the customer already tried, so you don't repeat it. If calls drop everywhere, not just on Wi-Fi, use **Troubleshoot Dropped Calls** instead.

* * *

## 

**Turn on Wi-Fi calling**

Go to **Settings** > **Cellular** > **Wi-Fi Calling** and turn on **Wi-Fi Calling on This iPhone**. It can take a few minutes to activate. On some phones the menu is called **Mobile Service**.

* * *

## 

**Forget the network and join it again**

Go to **Settings** > **Wi-Fi**, tap the info icon next to the network, tap **Forget This Network**, then join it again with the password.

* * *

## 

**Still not working?**

If the steps above didn't help, try these next, in this order.

**Restart the phone**

Press and hold the side button and either volume button until the slider appears, drag it, then turn the phone back on. Restarting clears minor glitches.

**Reset network settings**

Go to **Settings** > **General** > **Transfer or Reset iPhone** > **Reset** > **Reset Network Settings**. This clears saved Wi-Fi networks and passwords, Bluetooth pairings and VPN settings, so get the customer's OK before they start.

On iPhone 8 and earlier, press and hold the top button instead of the side button to restart.

* * *

**Check the fix:** Have the customer turn on Airplane mode with Wi-Fi on, then make a test call. A step can look like it worked before it really has.

If none of this helps, connect the customer with a specialist. Last reviewed 2026. Written for iOS 26. Related: Turn Airplane mode on or off, Reset network settings, Back up your phone.

# **Troubleshoot Dropped Calls - iOS**

When calls keep cutting out, the phone is usually losing its connection to the network for a moment. A weak signal, an old setting or a software glitch are the usual causes. Work through the sections below in order, and check the fix after each one.

* * *

## 

**Before you start**

Find out what the customer already tried, so you don't repeat it. If calls only drop at home and the customer uses Wi-Fi calling there, use **Troubleshoot Wi-Fi Calling** instead.

* * *

## 

**Turn Airplane mode on and off**

Open **Control Center** by swiping down from the top-right corner, tap the airplane icon, wait 10 seconds, then tap it again. This makes the phone reconnect to the network.

* * *

## 

**Restart the phone**

Press and hold the side button and either volume button until the slider appears, drag it, then turn the phone back on. Restarting clears minor glitches.

* * *

## 

**Still not working?**

If the steps above didn't help, try these next, in this order.

**Update the software**

Go to **Settings** > **General** > **Software Update** and install anything available.

**Reset network settings**

Go to **Settings** > **General** > **Transfer or Reset iPhone** > **Reset** > **Reset Network Settings**. This clears saved Wi-Fi networks and passwords, Bluetooth pairings and VPN settings, so get the customer's OK before they start.

On iPhone 8 and earlier, press and hold the top button instead of the side button to restart.

**Check the fix:** Have the customer make a test call and stay on it for two minutes. A step can look like it worked before it really has.

**Before you start**

* * *

**Restart the phone**

**Still not working?**

Wi-Fi calling lets the phone make calls over Wi-Fi where the signal is weak. When it stops working, calls at home drop or won't connect. Work through the sections below in order, and check the fix after each one.

* * *

## 

**Before you start**

Find out what the customer already tried, so you don't repeat it. If calls drop everywhere, not just on Wi-Fi, use **Troubleshoot Dropped Calls** instead.

* * *

## 

**Turn on Wi-Fi calling**

Go to **Settings** > **Cellular** > **Wi-Fi Calling** and turn on **Wi-Fi Calling on This iPhone**. It can take a few minutes to activate. On some phones the menu is called **Mobile Service**.

* * *

## 

**Forget the network and join it again**

Go to **Settings** > **Wi-Fi**, tap the info icon next to the network, tap **Forget This Network**, then join it again with the password.

* * *

## 

**Still not working?**

If the steps above didn't help, try these next, in this order.

**Restart the phone**

Press and hold the side button and either volume button until the slider appears, drag it, then turn the phone back on. Restarting clears minor glitches.

**Reset network settings**

Go to **Settings** > **General** > **Transfer or Reset iPhone** > **Reset** > **Reset Network Settings**. This clears saved Wi-Fi networks and passwords, Bluetooth pairings and VPN settings, so get the customer's OK before they start.

On iPhone 8 and earlier, press and hold the top button instead of the side button to restart.

* * *

**Check the fix:** Have the customer turn on Airplane mode with Wi-Fi on, then make a test call. A step can look like it worked before it really has.

If none of this helps, connect the customer with a specialist. Last reviewed 2023. Written for iOS 16 and 17; menus moved in later versions. Related: Turn Airplane mode on or off, Reset network settings, Back up your phone.

## 

**Before you start**

## 

**Turn on Wi-Fi calling**

* * *

## 

**Forget the network and join it again**

## 

**Still not working?**

=== KB-132: Troubleshoot Dropped Calls - iOS (In-Store) ===
# **Troubleshoot Dropped Calls - iOS**

When calls keep cutting out, the phone is usually losing its connection to the network for a moment. A weak signal, an old setting or a software glitch are the usual causes. For in-store technicians with diagnostic tools only. Don't use this article on a phone or chat call. Work through the sections below in order, and check the fix after each one.

* * *

## 

**Before you start**

Find out what the customer already tried, so you don't repeat it. If calls only drop at home and the customer uses Wi-Fi calling there, use **Troubleshoot Wi-Fi Calling** instead.

* * *

## 

**Turn Airplane mode on and off**

Open **Control Center** by swiping down from the top-right corner, tap the airplane icon, wait 10 seconds, then tap it again. This makes the phone reconnect to the network.

* * *

## 

**Restart the phone**

Press and hold the side button and either volume button until the slider appears, drag it, then turn the phone back on. Restarting clears minor glitches.

* * *

## 

**Still not working?**

If the steps above didn't help, try these next, in this order.

**Update the software**

Go to **Settings** > **General** > **Software Update** and install anything available.

**Reset network settings**

Go to **Settings** > **General** > **Transfer or Reset iPhone** > **Reset** > **Reset Network Settings**. This clears saved Wi-Fi networks and passwords, Bluetooth pairings and VPN settings, so get the customer's OK before they start.

On iPhone 8 and earlier, press and hold the top button instead of the side button to restart.

* * *

**Check the fix:** Have the customer make a test call and stay on it for two minutes. A step can look like it worked before it really has.

If none of this helps, connect the customer with a specialist. Last reviewed 2026. Written for iOS 26. Related: Turn Airplane mode on or off, Reset network settings, Back up your phone.

# **Troubleshoot Mobile Data - iOS**

When mobile data stops working, apps and websites only load on Wi-Fi. Most of the time a setting or a stuck connection is to blame, and a few quick steps get it working again. Work through the sections below in order, and check the fix after each one.

**Before you start**

* * *

**Check that mobile data is turned on**

Go to **Settings** > **Cellular** and make sure **Cellular Data** is turned on. On some phones this menu is called **Mobile Service** instead of **Cellular**; the switch is in the same place. If it's already on, move on to the next section.

* * *

## 

**Turn Airplane mode on and off**

* * *

## 

**Still not working?**

**Restart the phone**

# **Troubleshoot Dropped Calls - iOS**

When calls keep cutting out, the phone is usually losing its connection to the network for a moment. A weak signal, an old setting or a software glitch are the usual causes. Work through the sections below in order, and check the fix after each one.

* * *

## 

**Before you start**

Find out what the customer already tried, so you don't repeat it. If calls only drop at home and the customer uses Wi-Fi calling there, use **Troubleshoot Wi-Fi Calling** instead.

* * *

## 

**Turn Airplane mode on and off**

Open **Control Center** by swiping down from the top-right corner, tap the airplane icon, wait 10 seconds, then tap it again. This makes the phone reconnect to the network.

* * *

## 

**Restart the phone**

Press and hold the side button and either volume button until the slider appears, drag it, then turn the phone back on. Restarting clears minor glitches.

* * *

## 

**Still not working?**

If the steps above didn't help, try these next, in this order.

**Update the software**

Go to **Settings** > **General** > **Software Update** and install anything available.

**Reset network settings**

Go to **Settings** > **General** > **Transfer or Reset iPhone** > **Reset** > **Reset Network Settings**. This clears saved Wi-Fi networks and passwords, Bluetooth pairings and VPN settings, so get the customer's OK before they start.

On iPhone 8 and earlier, press and hold the top button instead of the side button to restart.

* * *

**Check the fix:** Have the customer make a test call and stay on it for two minutes. A step can look like it worked before it really has.

When the hotspot stops working, other devices can't get online through the phone. The phone's own data may still work. Work through the sections below in order, and check the fix after each one.

* * *

## 

**Before you start**

Find out what the customer already tried, so you don't repeat it. If the phone itself has no mobile data either, use **Troubleshoot Mobile Data** instead.

* * *

## 

**Turn the hotspot off and on**

Go to **Settings** > **Personal Hotspot**, turn off **Allow Others to Join**, wait 10 seconds, then turn it back on.

* * *

## 

**Restart the phone**

Press and hold the side button and either volume button until the slider appears, drag it, then turn the phone back on. Restarting clears minor glitches.

* * *

## 

**Still not working?**

If the steps above didn't help, try these next, in this order.

**Update the software**

Go to **Settings** > **General** > **Software Update** and install anything available.

**Reset network settings**

Go to **Settings** > **General** > **Transfer or Reset iPhone** > **Reset** > **Reset Network Settings**. This clears saved Wi-Fi networks and passwords, Bluetooth pairings and VPN settings, so get the customer's OK before they start.

On iPhone 8 and earlier, press and hold the top button instead of the side button to restart.

* * *

**Check the fix:** Have the customer connect their laptop to the hotspot and open a website. A step can look like it worked before it really has.

If none of this helps, connect the customer with a specialist. Last reviewed 2026. Written for iOS 26. Related: Turn Airplane mode on or off, Reset network settings, Back up your phone.

**Before you start**

* * *

**Turn Airplane mode on and off**

Open **Control Center** by swiping down from the top-right corner, tap the airplane icon, wait 10 seconds, then tap it again. This makes the phone reconnect to the network.

* * *

## 

**Restart the phone**

Press and hold the side button and either volume button until the slider appears, drag it, then turn the phone back on. Restarting clears minor glitches.

* * *

## 

**Still not working?**

If the steps above didn't help, try these next, in this order.

**Update the software**

Go to **Settings** > **General** > **Software Update** and install anything available.

**Reset network settings**

Go to **Settings** > **General** > **Transfer or Reset iPhone** > **Reset** > **Reset Network Settings**. This clears saved Wi-Fi networks and passwords, Bluetooth pairings and VPN settings, so get the customer's OK before they start.

On iPhone 8 and earlier, press and hold the top button instead of the side button to restart.

* * *

**Check the fix:** Have the customer make a test call and stay on it for two minutes. A step can look like it worked before it really has.

* * *

## 

**Before you start**

Find out what the customer already tried, so you don't repeat it. If there's an outage in the customer's area, no step here will help; check the outage map first.

* * *

## 

**Turn Airplane mode on and off**

Open **Control Center** by swiping down from the top-right corner, tap the airplane icon, wait 10 seconds, then tap it again. This makes the phone reconnect to the network.

* * *

## 

**Make sure the line is turned on**

Go to **Settings** > **Cellular**, tap the line under SIMs, and make sure **Turn On This Line** is on. On some phones the menu is called **Mobile Service**.

* * *

## 

**Still not working?**

If the steps above didn't help, try these next, in this order.

**Restart the phone**

Press and hold the side button and either volume button until the slider appears, drag it, then turn the phone back on. Restarting clears minor glitches.

=== KB-106: Troubleshoot No Service - iOS ===
# **Troubleshoot No Service - iOS**

When the phone shows **No Service** or **SOS**, it can't make calls, send texts or use mobile data. It's often a temporary network or SIM issue. Work through the sections below in order, and check the fix after each one.

* * *

## 

**Before you start**

Find out what the customer already tried, so you don't repeat it. If there's an outage in the customer's area, no step here will help; check the outage map first.

* * *

## 

**Turn Airplane mode on and off**

Open **Control Center** by swiping down from the top-right corner, tap the airplane icon, wait 10 seconds, then tap it again. This makes the phone reconnect to the network.

* * *

## 

**Make sure the line is turned on**

Go to **Settings** > **Cellular**, tap the line under SIMs, and make sure **Turn On This Line** is on. On some phones the menu is called **Mobile Service**.

* * *

## 

**Still not working?**

If the steps above didn't help, try these next, in this order.

**Restart the phone**

Press and hold the side button and either volume button until the slider appears, drag it, then turn the phone back on. Restarting clears minor glitches.

**Reset network settings**

Go to **Settings** > **General** > **Transfer or Reset iPhone** > **Reset** > **Reset Network Settings**. This clears saved Wi-Fi networks and passwords, Bluetooth pairings and VPN settings, so get the customer's OK before they start.

On iPhone 8 and earlier, press and hold the top button instead of the side button to restart.

* * *

**Check the fix:** Have the customer make a test call to another number. A step can look like it worked before it really has.

If none of this helps, connect the customer with a specialist. Last reviewed 2026. Written for iOS 26. Related: Turn Airplane mode on or off, Reset network settings, Back up your phone.

**Update the software**

# **Troubleshoot Dropped Calls - iOS**

When calls keep cutting out, the phone is usually losing its connection to the network for a moment. A weak signal, an old setting or a software glitch are the usual causes. Work through the sections below in order, and check the fix after each one.

* * *

## 

**Before you start**

Find out what the customer already tried, so you don't repeat it. If calls only drop at home and the customer uses Wi-Fi calling there, use **Troubleshoot Wi-Fi Calling** instead.

* * *

## 

**Turn Airplane mode on and off**

Open **Control Center** by swiping down from the top-right corner, tap the airplane icon, wait 10 seconds, then tap it again. This makes the phone reconnect to the network.

* * *

## 

**Restart the phone**

Press and hold the side button and either volume button until the slider appears, drag it, then turn the phone back on. Restarting clears minor glitches.

* * *

## 

**Still not working?**

If the steps above didn't help, try these next, in this order.

**Update the software**

Go to **Settings** > **General** > **Software Update** and install anything available.

# **Troubleshoot Wi-Fi Calling - iOS**

Wi-Fi calling lets the phone make calls over Wi-Fi where the signal is weak. When it stops working, calls at home drop or won't connect. Work through the sections below in order, and check the fix after each one.

* * *

## 

**Before you start**

Find out what the customer already tried, so you don't repeat it. If calls drop everywhere, not just on Wi-Fi, use **Troubleshoot Dropped Calls** instead.

* * *

## 

**Turn on Wi-Fi calling**

Go to **Settings** > **Cellular** > **Wi-Fi Calling** and turn on **Wi-Fi Calling on This iPhone**. It can take a few minutes to activate. On some phones the menu is called **Mobile Service**.

# **Troubleshoot Wi-Fi Calling - iOS**

**Before you start**

* * *

## 

**Turn on Wi-Fi calling**

* * *

## 

**Forget the network and join it again**

* * *

## 

**Still not working?**

**Restart the phone**

When text or picture messages won't send, they stay stuck with a red mark or a 'Not Delivered' note. Settings and network glitches are the usual causes. Work through the sections below in order, and check the fix after each one.

* * *

## 

**Before you start**

Find out what the customer already tried, so you don't repeat it. If only messages to one person fail, the problem may be on their side; ask them to check their phone first.

* * *

## 

**Check the messaging settings**

**Samsung Galaxy devices:** Open **Messages**, tap the three dots > **Settings** > **More settings** > **Multimedia messages**, and turn on **Auto retrieve**. **Other Android devices (Pixel):** Open **Messages**, tap your profile picture > **Messages settings** > **Advanced**, and turn on **Auto-download MMS**.

* * *

## 

**Turn Airplane mode on and off**

**Samsung Galaxy devices:** Swipe down twice from the top of the screen, tap **Airplane mode**, wait 10 seconds, then tap it again. **Other Android devices (Pixel):** Swipe down from the top of the screen, tap **Airplane mode**, wait 10 seconds, then tap it again.

* * *

## 

**Still not working?**

If the steps above didn't help, try these next, in this order.

**Update the software**

**Samsung Galaxy devices:** Go to **Settings** > **Software update** > **Download and install**. **Other Android devices (Pixel):** Go to **Settings** > **System** > **Software updates**.

**Reset network settings**

**Samsung Galaxy devices:** Go to **Settings** > **General management** > **Reset** > **Reset network settings**. **Other Android devices (Pixel):** Go to **Settings** > **System** > **Reset options** > **Reset Wi-Fi, mobile & Bluetooth**. This clears saved Wi-Fi networks and passwords and Bluetooth pairings, so get the customer's OK before they start.

On older Samsung phones, **Data usage** may be under **Settings** > **Connections** > **Mobile networks**.

* * *

**Check the fix:** Have the customer send a test message to someone they know. A step can look like it worked before it really has.

If none of this helps, connect the customer with a specialist. Last reviewed 2026. Written for Android 16. Related: Turn Airplane mode on or off, Reset network settings, Back up your phone.

=== KB-124: Troubleshoot Picture and Group Messages - iOS ===
# **Troubleshoot Picture and Group Messages - iOS**

Picture messages and group texts need mobile data, even when regular texts work. When they fail, the photo shows a red mark or 'Not Delivered'. Work through the sections below in order, and check the fix after each one.

* * *

## 

**Before you start**

Find out what the customer already tried, so you don't repeat it. If regular one-to-one texts fail too, this isn't a picture message problem: use **Troubleshoot Messaging** instead.

* * *

## 

**Check that mobile data is turned on**

Go to **Settings** > **Cellular** and make sure **Cellular Data** is turned on. On some phones this menu is called **Mobile Service** instead of **Cellular**; the switch is in the same place. If it's already on, move on to the next section.

* * *

## 

**Check the messaging settings**

Go to **Settings** > **Apps** > **Messages** and make sure **MMS Messaging** and **Send as Text Message** are on.

* * *

## 

**Still not working?**

If the steps above didn't help, try these next, in this order.

**Restart the phone**

Press and hold the side button and either volume button until the slider appears, drag it, then turn the phone back on. Restarting clears minor glitches.

**Reset network settings**

Go to **Settings** > **General** > **Transfer or Reset iPhone** > **Reset** > **Reset Network Settings**. This clears saved Wi-Fi networks and passwords, Bluetooth pairings and VPN settings, so get the customer's OK before they start.

On iPhone 8 and earlier, press and hold the top button instead of the side button to restart.

* * *

**Check the fix:** Have the customer send a photo to someone they know. A step can look like it worked before it really has.

If none of this helps, connect the customer with a specialist. Last reviewed 2026. Written for iOS 26. Related: Turn Airplane mode on or off, Reset network settings, Back up your phone.

=== KB-130: Troubleshoot Dropped Calls - iOS ===
# **Troubleshoot Dropped Calls - iOS**

When calls keep cutting out, the phone is usually losing its connection to the network for a moment. A weak signal, an old setting or a software glitch are the usual causes. Work through the sections below in order, and check the fix after each one.

* * *

## 

**Before you start**

Find out what the customer already tried, so you don't repeat it. If calls only drop at home and the customer uses Wi-Fi calling there, use **Troubleshoot Wi-Fi Calling** instead.

* * *

## 

**Turn Airplane mode on and off**

Open **Control Center** by swiping down from the top-right corner, tap the airplane icon, wait 10 seconds, then tap it again. This makes the phone reconnect to the network.

* * *

## 

**Restart the phone**

Press and hold the side button and either volume button until the slider appears, drag it, then turn the phone back on. Restarting clears minor glitches.

* * *

## 

**Still not working?**

If the steps above didn't help, try these next, in this order.

**Update the software**

Go to **Settings** > **General** > **Software Update** and install anything available.

**Reset network settings**

Go to **Settings** > **General** > **Transfer or Reset iPhone** > **Reset** > **Reset Network Settings**. This clears saved Wi-Fi networks and passwords, Bluetooth pairings and VPN settings, so get the customer's OK before they start.

On iPhone 8 and earlier, press and hold the top button instead of the side button to restart.

* * *

**Check the fix:** Have the customer make a test call and stay on it for two minutes. A step can look like it worked before it really has.

If none of this helps, connect the customer with a specialist. Last reviewed 2026. Written for iOS 26. Related: Turn Airplane mode on or off, Reset network settings, Back up your phone.

=== KB-130: Troubleshoot Dropped Calls - iOS ===
# **Troubleshoot Dropped Calls - iOS**

When calls keep cutting out, the phone is usually losing its connection to the network for a moment. A weak signal, an old setting or a software glitch are the usual causes. Work through the sections below in order, and check the fix after each one.

* * *

## 

**Before you start**

Find out what the customer already tried, so you don't repeat it. If calls only drop at home and the customer uses Wi-Fi calling there, use **Troubleshoot Wi-Fi Calling** instead.

* * *

## 

**Turn Airplane mode on and off**

Open **Control Center** by swiping down from the top-right corner, tap the airplane icon, wait 10 seconds, then tap it again. This makes the phone reconnect to the network.

* * *

## 

**Restart the phone**

Press and hold the side button and either volume button until the slider appears, drag it, then turn the phone back on. Restarting clears minor glitches.

* * *

## 

**Still not working?**

If the steps above didn't help, try these next, in this order.

**Update the software**

Go to **Settings** > **General** > **Software Update** and install anything available.

**Reset network settings**

Go to **Settings** > **General** > **Transfer or Reset iPhone** > **Reset** > **Reset Network Settings**. This clears saved Wi-Fi networks and passwords, Bluetooth pairings and VPN settings, so get the customer's OK before they start.

On iPhone 8 and earlier, press and hold the top button instead of the side button to restart.

* * *

**Check the fix:** Have the customer make a test call and stay on it for two minutes. A step can look like it worked before it really has.

For in-store technicians with diagnostic tools only. Don't use this article on a phone or chat call. Work through the sections below in order, and check the fix after each one.

* * *

## 

**Before you start**

Find out what the customer already tried, so you don't repeat it. If the phone shows **SOS** or **No Service** at the top of the screen, this isn't a mobile data problem: use **Troubleshoot No Service** instead.

* * *

## 

**Check that mobile data is turned on**

**Samsung Galaxy devices:** Go to **Settings** > **Connections** > **Data usage** and turn on **Mobile data**. **Other Android devices (Pixel):** Go to **Settings** > **Network & internet** > **SIMs** and turn on **Mobile data**. If it's already on, move on to the next section.

* * *

## 

**Turn Airplane mode on and off**

**Samsung Galaxy devices:** Swipe down twice from the top of the screen, tap **Airplane mode**, wait 10 seconds, then tap it again. **Other Android devices (Pixel):** Swipe down from the top of the screen, tap **Airplane mode**, wait 10 seconds, then tap it again.

* * *

## 

**Still not working?**

If the steps above didn't help, try these next, in this order.

**Restart the phone**

**Samsung Galaxy devices:** Press and hold the **Side key**, tap **Power off** > **Restart**. **Other Android devices (Pixel):** Press and hold the **Power** button, then tap **Restart**.

**Reset network settings**

**Samsung Galaxy devices:** Go to **Settings** > **General management** > **Reset** > **Reset network settings**. **Other Android devices (Pixel):** Go to **Settings** > **System** > **Reset options** > **Reset Wi-Fi, mobile & Bluetooth**. This clears saved Wi-Fi networks and passwords and Bluetooth pairings, so get the customer's OK before they start.

On older Samsung phones, **Data usage** may be under **Settings** > **Connections** > **Mobile networks**.

* * *

**Check the fix:** Have the customer turn off Wi-Fi and open a website. An LTE or 5G icon coming back doesn't mean data works. A step can look like it worked before it really has.

If none of this helps, connect the customer with a specialist. Last reviewed 2026. Written for Android 16. Related: Turn Airplane mode on or off, Reset network settings, Back up your phone.

=== KB-130: Troubleshoot Dropped Calls - iOS ===
# **Troubleshoot Dropped Calls - iOS**

When calls keep cutting out, the phone is usually losing its connection to the network for a moment. A weak signal, an old setting or a software glitch are the usual causes. Work through the sections below in order, and check the fix after each one.

* * *

## 

**Before you start**

Find out what the customer already tried, so you don't repeat it. If calls only drop at home and the customer uses Wi-Fi calling there, use **Troubleshoot Wi-Fi Calling** instead.

* * *

## 

**Turn Airplane mode on and off**

Open **Control Center** by swiping down from the top-right corner, tap the airplane icon, wait 10 seconds, then tap it again. This makes the phone reconnect to the network.

* * *

## 

**Restart the phone**

Press and hold the side button and either volume button until the slider appears, drag it, then turn the phone back on. Restarting clears minor glitches.

* * *

## 

**Still not working?**

If the steps above didn't help, try these next, in this order.

**Update the software**

Go to **Settings** > **General** > **Software Update** and install anything available.

**Reset network settings**

Go to **Settings** > **General** > **Transfer or Reset iPhone** > **Reset** > **Reset Network Settings**. This clears saved Wi-Fi networks and passwords, Bluetooth pairings and VPN settings, so get the customer's OK before they start.

On iPhone 8 and earlier, press and hold the top button instead of the side button to restart.

* * *

**Check the fix:** Have the customer make a test call and stay on it for two minutes. A step can look like it worked before it really has.

If none of this helps, connect the customer with a specialist. Last reviewed 2026. Written for iOS 26. Related: Turn Airplane mode on or off, Reset network settings, Back up your phone.

# **Troubleshoot Wi-Fi Calling - iOS**

Wi-Fi calling lets the phone make calls over Wi-Fi where the signal is weak. When it stops working, calls at home drop or won't connect. Work through the sections below in order, and check the fix after each one.

## 

**Before you start**

Find out what the customer already tried, so you don't repeat it. If calls drop everywhere, not just on Wi-Fi, use **Troubleshoot Dropped Calls** instead.

* * *

## 

**Turn on Wi-Fi calling**

* * *

## 

**Forget the network and join it again**

Go to **Settings** > **Wi-Fi**, tap the info icon next to the network, tap **Forget This Network**, then join it again with the password.

* * *

## 

**Still not working?**

If the steps above didn't help, try these next, in this order.

**Restart the phone**

Press and hold the side button and either volume button until the slider appears, drag it, then turn the phone back on. Restarting clears minor glitches.

**Reset network settings**

Go to **Settings** > **General** > **Transfer or Reset iPhone** > **Reset** > **Reset Network Settings**. This clears saved Wi-Fi networks and passwords, Bluetooth pairings and VPN settings, so get the customer's OK before they start.

On iPhone 8 and earlier, press and hold the top button instead of the side button to restart.

* * *

**Check the fix:** Have the customer turn on Airplane mode with Wi-Fi on, then make a test call. A step can look like it worked before it really has.

If none of this helps, connect the customer with a specialist. Last reviewed 2026. Written for iOS 26. Related: Turn Airplane mode on or off, Reset network settings, Back up your phone.

=== KB-132: Troubleshoot Dropped Calls - iOS (In-Store) ===
# **Troubleshoot Dropped Calls - iOS**

When calls keep cutting out, the phone is usually losing its connection to the network for a moment. A weak signal, an old setting or a software glitch are the usual causes. * * *

## 

**Before you start**

Find out what the customer already tried, so you don't repeat it. If calls only drop at home and the customer uses Wi-Fi calling there, use **Troubleshoot Wi-Fi Calling** instead.

* * *

## 

**Turn Airplane mode on and off**

Open **Control Center** by swiping down from the top-right corner, tap the airplane icon, wait 10 seconds, then tap it again. This makes the phone reconnect to the network.

* * *

## 

**Restart the phone**

Press and hold the side button and either volume button until the slider appears, drag it, then turn the phone back on. Restarting clears minor glitches.

* * *

## 

**Still not working?**

If the steps above didn't help, try these next, in this order.

**Update the software**

Go to **Settings** > **General** > **Software Update** and install anything available.

**Reset network settings**

Go to **Settings** > **General** > **Transfer or Reset iPhone** > **Reset** > **Reset Network Settings**. This clears saved Wi-Fi networks and passwords, Bluetooth pairings and VPN settings, so get the customer's OK before they start.

On iPhone 8 and earlier, press and hold the top button instead of the side button to restart.

* * *

**Check the fix:** Have the customer make a test call and stay on it for two minutes. A step can look like it worked before it really has.

If none of this helps, connect the customer with a specialist. Last reviewed 2026. Written for iOS 26. Related: Turn Airplane mode on or off, Reset network settings, Back up your phone.

=== KB-138: Troubleshoot Wi-Fi Calling - iOS (In-Store) ===
# **Troubleshoot Wi-Fi Calling - iOS**

Wi-Fi calling lets the phone make calls over Wi-Fi where the signal is weak. When it stops working, calls at home drop or won't connect. For in-store technicians with diagnostic tools only. Don't use this article on a phone or chat call. Work through the sections below in order, and check the fix after each one.

* * *

## 

**Before you start**

Find out what the customer already tried, so you don't repeat it. If calls drop everywhere, not just on Wi-Fi, use **Troubleshoot Dropped Calls** instead.

* * *

## 

**Turn on Wi-Fi calling**

Go to **Settings** > **Cellular** > **Wi-Fi Calling** and turn on **Wi-Fi Calling on This iPhone**. It can take a few minutes to activate. On some phones the menu is called **Mobile Service**.

* * *

## 

**Forget the network and join it again**

Go to **Settings** > **Wi-Fi**, tap the info icon next to the network, tap **Forget This Network**, then join it again with the password.

* * *

## 

**Still not working?**

If the steps above didn't help, try these next, in this order.

**Restart the phone**

Press and hold the side button and either volume button until the slider appears, drag it, then turn the phone back on. Restarting clears minor glitches.

**Reset network settings**

Go to **Settings** > **General** > **Transfer or Reset iPhone** > **Reset** > **Reset Network Settings**. This clears saved Wi-Fi networks and passwords, Bluetooth pairings and VPN settings, so get the customer's OK before they start.

On iPhone 8 and earlier, press and hold the top button instead of the side button to restart.

* * *

**Check the fix:** Have the customer turn on Airplane mode with Wi-Fi on, then make a test call. A step can look like it worked before it really has.

If none of this helps, connect the customer with a specialist. Last reviewed 2026. Written for iOS 26. Related: Turn Airplane mode on or off, Reset network settings, Back up your phone.

=== KB-130: Troubleshoot Dropped Calls - iOS ===
# **Troubleshoot Dropped Calls - iOS**

When calls keep cutting out, the phone is usually losing its connection to the network for a moment. A weak signal, an old setting or a software glitch are the usual causes. Work through the sections below in order, and check the fix after each one.

* * *

## 

**Before you start**

Find out what the customer already tried, so you don't repeat it. If calls only drop at home and the customer uses Wi-Fi calling there, use **Troubleshoot Wi-Fi Calling** instead.

* * *

## 

**Turn Airplane mode on and off**

Open **Control Center** by swiping down from the top-right corner, tap the airplane icon, wait 10 seconds, then tap it again. This makes the phone reconnect to the network.

* * *

## 

**Restart the phone**

Press and hold the side button and either volume button until the slider appears, drag it, then turn the phone back on. Restarting clears minor glitches.

* * *

## 

**Still not working?**

If the steps above didn't help, try these next, in this order.

**Update the software**

Go to **Settings** > **General** > **Software Update** and install anything available.

**Reset network settings**

Go to **Settings** > **General** > **Transfer or Reset iPhone** > **Reset** > **Reset Network Settings**. This clears saved Wi-Fi networks and passwords, Bluetooth pairings and VPN settings, so get the customer's OK before they start.

On iPhone 8 and earlier, press and hold the top button instead of the side button to restart.

* * *

**Check the fix:** Have the customer make a test call and stay on it for two minutes. A step can look like it worked before it really has.

If none of this helps, connect the customer with a specialist. Last reviewed 2026. Written for iOS 26. Related: Turn Airplane mode on or off, Reset network settings, Back up your phone.

Wi-Fi calling lets the phone make calls over Wi-Fi where the signal is weak. When it stops working, calls at home drop or won't connect. Work through the sections below in order, and check the fix after each one.

* * *

## 

**Before you start**

Find out what the customer already tried, so you don't repeat it. If calls drop everywhere, not just on Wi-Fi, use **Troubleshoot Dropped Calls** instead.

* * *

## 

**Turn on Wi-Fi calling**

**Samsung Galaxy devices:** Open the **Phone** app, tap the three dots > **Settings**, and turn on **Wi-Fi calling**. **Other Android devices (Pixel):** Open the **Phone** app, tap the three dots > **Settings** > **Calls** > **Wi-Fi calling**, and turn it on.

* * *

## 

**Forget the network and join it again**

**Samsung Galaxy devices:** Go to **Settings** > **Connections** > **Wi-Fi**, tap the gear next to the network, tap **Forget**, then join it again. **Other Android devices (Pixel):** Go to **Settings** > **Network & internet** > **Internet**, tap the network, tap **Forget**, then join it again.

* * *

## 

**Still not working?**

If the steps above didn't help, try these next, in this order.

**Restart the phone**

**Samsung Galaxy devices:** Press and hold the **Side key**, tap **Power off** > **Restart**. **Other Android devices (Pixel):** Press and hold the **Power** button, then tap **Restart**.

**Reset network settings**

**Samsung Galaxy devices:** Go to **Settings** > **General management** > **Reset** > **Reset network settings**. **Other Android devices (Pixel):** Go to **Settings** > **System** > **Reset options** > **Reset Wi-Fi, mobile & Bluetooth**. This clears saved Wi-Fi networks and passwords and Bluetooth pairings, so get the customer's OK before they start.

On older Samsung phones, **Data usage** may be under **Settings** > **Connections** > **Mobile networks**.

* * *

**Check the fix:** Have the customer turn on Airplane mode with Wi-Fi on, then make a test call. A step can look like it worked before it really has.

If none of this helps, connect the customer with a specialist. Last reviewed 2023. Written for Android 13; menus moved in later versions. Related: Turn Airplane mode on or off, Reset network settings, Back up your phone.

=== KB-130: Troubleshoot Dropped Calls - iOS ===
# **Troubleshoot Dropped Calls - iOS**

When calls keep cutting out, the phone is usually losing its connection to the network for a moment. A weak signal, an old setting or a software glitch are the usual causes. Work through the sections below in order, and check the fix after each one.

* * *

## 

**Before you start**

Find out what the customer already tried, so you don't repeat it. If calls only drop at home and the customer uses Wi-Fi calling there, use **Troubleshoot Wi-Fi Calling** instead.

* * *

## 

**Turn Airplane mode on and off**

Open **Control Center** by swiping down from the top-right corner, tap the airplane icon, wait 10 seconds, then tap it again. This makes the phone reconnect to the network.

* * *

## 

**Restart the phone**

Press and hold the side button and either volume button until the slider appears, drag it, then turn the phone back on. Restarting clears minor glitches.

* * *

## 

**Still not working?**

If the steps above didn't help, try these next, in this order.

**Update the software**

Go to **Settings** > **General** > **Software Update** and install anything available.

**Reset network settings**

Go to **Settings** > **General** > **Transfer or Reset iPhone** > **Reset** > **Reset Network Settings**. This clears saved Wi-Fi networks and passwords, Bluetooth pairings and VPN settings, so get the customer's OK before they start.

On iPhone 8 and earlier, press and hold the top button instead of the side button to restart.

* * *

**Check the fix:** Have the customer make a test call and stay on it for two minutes. A step can look like it worked before it really has.

If none of this helps, connect the customer with a specialist. Last reviewed 2026. Written for iOS 26. Related: Turn Airplane mode on or off, Reset network settings, Back up your phone.

# **Troubleshoot Mobile Data - iOS**

When mobile data stops working, apps and websites only load on Wi-Fi. Most of the time a setting or a stuck connection is to blame, and a few quick steps get it working again. Work through the sections below in order, and check the fix after each one.

* * *

## 

**Before you start**

Find out what the customer already tried, so you don't repeat it. If the phone shows **SOS** or **No Service** at the top of the screen, this isn't a mobile data problem: use **Troubleshoot No Service** instead.

* * *

## 

**Check that mobile data is turned on**

Go to **Settings** > **Cellular** and make sure **Cellular Data** is turned on. On some phones this menu is called **Mobile Service** instead of **Cellular**; the switch is in the same place. If it's already on, move on to the next section.

* * *

## 

**Turn Airplane mode on and off**

Open **Control Center** by swiping down from the top-right corner, tap the airplane icon, wait 10 seconds, then tap it again. This makes the phone reconnect to the network.

* * *

## 

**Still not working?**

If the steps above didn't help, try these next, in this order.

**Restart the phone**

Press and hold the side button and either volume button until the slider appears, drag it, then turn the phone back on. Restarting clears minor glitches.

**Reset network settings**

Go to **Settings** > **General** > **Transfer or Reset iPhone** > **Reset** > **Reset Network Settings**. This clears saved Wi-Fi networks and passwords, Bluetooth pairings and VPN settings, so get the customer's OK before they start.

On iPhone 8 and earlier, press and hold the top button instead of the side button to restart.

* * *

**Check the fix:** Have the customer turn off Wi-Fi and open a website. An LTE or 5G icon coming back doesn't mean data works. A step can look like it worked before it really has.

If none of this helps, connect the customer with a specialist. Last reviewed 2026. Written for iOS 26. Related: Turn Airplane mode on or off, Reset network settings, Back up your phone.

=== KB-130: Troubleshoot Dropped Calls - iOS ===
# **Troubleshoot Dropped Calls - iOS**

When calls keep cutting out, the phone is usually losing its connection to the network for a moment. A weak signal, an old setting or a software glitch are the usual causes. Work through the sections below in order, and check the fix after each one.

* * *

## 

**Before you start**

Find out what the customer already tried, so you don't repeat it. If calls only drop at home and the customer uses Wi-Fi calling there, use **Troubleshoot Wi-Fi Calling** instead.

* * *

## 

**Turn Airplane mode on and off**

Open **Control Center** by swiping down from the top-right corner, tap the airplane icon, wait 10 seconds, then tap it again. This makes the phone reconnect to the network.

* * *

## 

**Restart the phone**

Press and hold the side button and either volume button until the slider appears, drag it, then turn the phone back on. Restarting clears minor glitches.

* * *

## 

**Still not working?**

If the steps above didn't help, try these next, in this order.

**Update the software**

Go to **Settings** > **General** > **Software Update** and install anything available.

**Reset network settings**

Go to **Settings** > **General** > **Transfer or Reset iPhone** > **Reset** > **Reset Network Settings**. This clears saved Wi-Fi networks and passwords, Bluetooth pairings and VPN settings, so get the customer's OK before they start.

On iPhone 8 and earlier, press and hold the top button instead of the side button to restart.

* * *

**Check the fix:** Have the customer make a test call and stay on it for two minutes. A step can look like it worked before it really has.

If none of this helps, connect the customer with a specialist. Last reviewed 2026. Written for iOS 26. Related: Turn Airplane mode on or off, Reset network settings, Back up your phone.

=== KB-100: Troubleshoot Mobile Data - iOS ===
# **Troubleshoot Mobile Data - iOS**

When mobile data stops working, apps and websites only load on Wi-Fi. Most of the time a setting or a stuck connection is to blame, and a few quick steps get it working again. Work through the sections below in order, and check the fix after each one.

* * *

## 

**Before you start**

Find out what the customer already tried, so you don't repeat it. If the phone shows **SOS** or **No Service** at the top of the screen, this isn't a mobile data problem: use **Troubleshoot No Service** instead.

* * *

## 

**Check that mobile data is turned on**

Go to **Settings** > **Cellular** and make sure **Cellular Data** is turned on. On some phones this menu is called **Mobile Service** instead of **Cellular**; the switch is in the same place. If it's already on, move on to the next section.

* * *

## 

**Turn Airplane mode on and off**

Open **Control Center** by swiping down from the top-right corner, tap the airplane icon, wait 10 seconds, then tap it again. This makes the phone reconnect to the network.

* * *

## 

**Still not working?**

If the steps above didn't help, try these next, in this order.

**Restart the phone**

Press and hold the side button and either volume button until the slider appears, drag it, then turn the phone back on. Restarting clears minor glitches.

**Reset network settings**

Go to **Settings** > **General** > **Transfer or Reset iPhone** > **Reset** > **Reset Network Settings**. This clears saved Wi-Fi networks and passwords, Bluetooth pairings and VPN settings, so get the customer's OK before they start.

On iPhone 8 and earlier, press and hold the top button instead of the side button to restart.

* * *

**Check the fix:** Have the customer turn off Wi-Fi and open a website. An LTE or 5G icon coming back doesn't mean data works. A step can look like it worked before it really has.

If none of this helps, connect the customer with a specialist. Last reviewed 2026. Written for iOS 26. Related: Turn Airplane mode on or off, Reset network settings, Back up your phone.

=== KB-130: Troubleshoot Dropped Calls - iOS ===
# **Troubleshoot Dropped Calls - iOS**

When calls keep cutting out, the phone is usually losing its connection to the network for a moment. A weak signal, an old setting or a software glitch are the usual causes. Work through the sections below in order, and check the fix after each one.

* * *

## 

**Before you start**

Find out what the customer already tried, so you don't repeat it. If calls only drop at home and the customer uses Wi-Fi calling there, use **Troubleshoot Wi-Fi Calling** instead.

* * *

## 

**Turn Airplane mode on and off**

Open **Control Center** by swiping down from the top-right corner, tap the airplane icon, wait 10 seconds, then tap it again. This makes the phone reconnect to the network.

* * *

## 

**Restart the phone**

Press and hold the side button and either volume button until the slider appears, drag it, then turn the phone back on. Restarting clears minor glitches.

* * *

## 

**Still not working?**

If the steps above didn't help, try these next, in this order.

**Update the software**

Go to **Settings** > **General** > **Software Update** and install anything available.

**Reset network settings**

Go to **Settings** > **General** > **Transfer or Reset iPhone** > **Reset** > **Reset Network Settings**. This clears saved Wi-Fi networks and passwords, Bluetooth pairings and VPN settings, so get the customer's OK before they start.

On iPhone 8 and earlier, press and hold the top button instead of the side button to restart.

* * *

**Check the fix:** Have the customer make a test call and stay on it for two minutes. A step can look like it worked before it really has.

If none of this helps, connect the customer with a specialist. Last reviewed 2026. Written for iOS 26. Related: Turn Airplane mode on or off, Reset network settings, Back up your phone.

When mobile data stops working, apps and websites only load on Wi-Fi. Most of the time a setting or a stuck connection is to blame, and a few quick steps get it working again. For in-store technicians with diagnostic tools only. Don't use this article on a phone or chat call. Work through the sections below in order, and check the fix after each one.

* * *

## 

**Before you start**

Find out what the customer already tried, so you don't repeat it. If the phone shows **SOS** or **No Service** at the top of the screen, this isn't a mobile data problem: use **Troubleshoot No Service** instead.

* * *

## 

**Check that mobile data is turned on**

**Samsung Galaxy devices:** Go to **Settings** > **Connections** > **Data usage** and turn on **Mobile data**. **Other Android devices (Pixel):** Go to **Settings** > **Network & internet** > **SIMs** and turn on **Mobile data**. If it's already on, move on to the next section.

* * *

## 

**Turn Airplane mode on and off**

**Samsung Galaxy devices:** Swipe down twice from the top of the screen, tap **Airplane mode**, wait 10 seconds, then tap it again. **Other Android devices (Pixel):** Swipe down from the top of the screen, tap **Airplane mode**, wait 10 seconds, then tap it again.

* * *

## 

**Still not working?**

If the steps above didn't help, try these next, in this order.

**Restart the phone**

**Samsung Galaxy devices:** Press and hold the **Side key**, tap **Power off** > **Restart**. **Other Android devices (Pixel):** Press and hold the **Power** button, then tap **Restart**.

**Reset network settings**

**Samsung Galaxy devices:** Go to **Settings** > **General management** > **Reset** > **Reset network settings**. **Other Android devices (Pixel):** Go to **Settings** > **System** > **Reset options** > **Reset Wi-Fi, mobile & Bluetooth**. This clears saved Wi-Fi networks and passwords and Bluetooth pairings, so get the customer's OK before they start.

On older Samsung phones, **Data usage** may be under **Settings** > **Connections** > **Mobile networks**.

* * *

**Check the fix:** Have the customer turn off Wi-Fi and open a website. An LTE or 5G icon coming back doesn't mean data works. A step can look like it worked before it really has.

If none of this helps, connect the customer with a specialist. Last reviewed 2026. Written for Android 16. Related: Turn Airplane mode on or off, Reset network settings, Back up your phone.

=== KB-130: Troubleshoot Dropped Calls - iOS ===
# **Troubleshoot Dropped Calls - iOS**

When calls keep cutting out, the phone is usually losing its connection to the network for a moment. A weak signal, an old setting or a software glitch are the usual causes. Work through the sections below in order, and check the fix after each one.

* * *

## 

**Before you start**

Find out what the customer already tried, so you don't repeat it. If calls only drop at home and the customer uses Wi-Fi calling there, use **Troubleshoot Wi-Fi Calling** instead.

* * *

## 

**Turn Airplane mode on and off**

Open **Control Center** by swiping down from the top-right corner, tap the airplane icon, wait 10 seconds, then tap it again. This makes the phone reconnect to the network.

* * *

## 

**Restart the phone**

Press and hold the side button and either volume button until the slider appears, drag it, then turn the phone back on. Restarting clears minor glitches.

* * *

## 

**Still not working?**

If the steps above didn't help, try these next, in this order.

**Update the software**

Go to **Settings** > **General** > **Software Update** and install anything available.

**Reset network settings**

Go to **Settings** > **General** > **Transfer or Reset iPhone** > **Reset** > **Reset Network Settings**. This clears saved Wi-Fi networks and passwords, Bluetooth pairings and VPN settings, so get the customer's OK before they start.

On iPhone 8 and earlier, press and hold the top button instead of the side button to restart.

* * *

**Check the fix:** Have the customer make a test call and stay on it for two minutes. A step can look like it worked before it really has.

If none of this helps, connect the customer with a specialist. Last reviewed 2026. Written for iOS 26. Related: Turn Airplane mode on or off, Reset network settings, Back up your phone.

=== KB-132: Troubleshoot Dropped Calls - iOS (In-Store) ===
# **Troubleshoot Dropped Calls - iOS**

When calls keep cutting out, the phone is usually losing its connection to the network for a moment. A weak signal, an old setting or a software glitch are the usual causes. For in-store technicians with diagnostic tools only. Don't use this article on a phone or chat call. Work through the sections below in order, and check the fix after each one.

* * *

## 

**Before you start**

Find out what the customer already tried, so you don't repeat it. If calls only drop at home and the customer uses Wi-Fi calling there, use **Troubleshoot Wi-Fi Calling** instead.

* * *

## 

**Turn Airplane mode on and off**

Open **Control Center** by swiping down from the top-right corner, tap the airplane icon, wait 10 seconds, then tap it again. This makes the phone reconnect to the network.

* * *

## 

**Restart the phone**

Press and hold the side button and either volume button until the slider appears, drag it, then turn the phone back on. Restarting clears minor glitches.

* * *

## 

**Still not working?**

If the steps above didn't help, try these next, in this order.

**Update the software**

Go to **Settings** > **General** > **Software Update** and install anything available.

**Reset network settings**

Go to **Settings** > **General** > **Transfer or Reset iPhone** > **Reset** > **Reset Network Settings**. This clears saved Wi-Fi networks and passwords, Bluetooth pairings and VPN settings, so get the customer's OK before they start.

On iPhone 8 and earlier, press and hold the top button instead of the side button to restart.

* * *

**Check the fix:** Have the customer make a test call and stay on it for two minutes. A step can look like it worked before it really has.

If none of this helps, connect the customer with a specialist. Last reviewed 2026. Written for iOS 26. Related: Turn Airplane mode on or off, Reset network settings, Back up your phone.

* * *

## 

**Turn Airplane mode on and off**

**Samsung Galaxy devices:** Swipe down twice from the top of the screen, tap **Airplane mode**, wait 10 seconds, then tap it again. **Other Android devices (Pixel):** Swipe down from the top of the screen, tap **Airplane mode**, wait 10 seconds, then tap it again.

* * *

## 

**Still not working?**

=== KB-108: Troubleshoot No Service - iOS (In-Store) ===
# **Troubleshoot No Service - iOS**

When the phone shows **No Service** or **SOS**, it can't make calls, send texts or use mobile data. It's often a temporary network or SIM issue. For in-store technicians with diagnostic tools only. Don't use this article on a phone or chat call. Work through the sections below in order, and check the fix after each one.

* * *

## 

**Before you start**

Find out what the customer already tried, so you don't repeat it. If there's an outage in the customer's area, no step here will help; check the outage map first.

* * *

## 

**Turn Airplane mode on and off**

Open **Control Center** by swiping down from the top-right corner, tap the airplane icon, wait 10 seconds, then tap it again. This makes the phone reconnect to the network.

* * *

## 

**Make sure the line is turned on**

Go to **Settings** > **Cellular**, tap the line under SIMs, and make sure **Turn On This Line** is on. On some phones the menu is called **Mobile Service**.

* * *

## 

**Still not working?**

If the steps above didn't help, try these next, in this order.

Press and hold the side button and either volume button until the slider appears, drag it, then turn the phone back on. Restarting clears minor glitches.

* * *

## 

**Before you start**

* * *

## 

**Turn on Wi-Fi calling**

Go to **Settings** > **Cellular** > **Wi-Fi Calling** and turn on **Wi-Fi Calling on This iPhone**. It can take a few minutes to activate. On some phones the menu is called **Mobile Service**.

* * *

## 

**Forget the network and join it again**

Go to **Settings** > **Wi-Fi**, tap the info icon next to the network, tap **Forget This Network**, then join it again with the password.

* * *

## 

**Still not working?**

If the steps above didn't help, try these next, in this order.

**Restart the phone**

Press and hold the side button and either volume button until the slider appears, drag it, then turn the phone back on. Restarting clears minor glitches.

**Reset network settings**

Go to **Settings** > **General** > **Transfer or Reset iPhone** > **Reset** > **Reset Network Settings**. This clears saved Wi-Fi networks and passwords, Bluetooth pairings and VPN settings, so get the customer's OK before they start.

On iPhone 8 and earlier, press and hold the top button instead of the side button to restart.

* * *

**Check the fix:** Have the customer turn on Airplane mode with Wi-Fi on, then make a test call. A step can look like it worked before it really has.

* * *

* * *

**Turn Airplane mode on and off**

* * *

## 

**Restart the phone**

Wi-Fi calling lets the phone make calls over Wi-Fi where the signal is weak. When it stops working, calls at home drop or won't connect. Work through the sections below in order, and check the fix after each one.

* * *

## 

**Before you start**

Find out what the customer already tried, so you don't repeat it. If calls drop everywhere, not just on Wi-Fi, use **Troubleshoot Dropped Calls** instead.

* * *

## 

**Turn on Wi-Fi calling**

Go to **Settings** > **Cellular** > **Wi-Fi Calling** and turn on **Wi-Fi Calling on This iPhone**. It can take a few minutes to activate. On some phones the menu is called **Mobile Service**.

* * *

## 

**Forget the network and join it again**

Go to **Settings** > **Wi-Fi**, tap the info icon next to the network, tap **Forget This Network**, then join it again with the password.

* * *

## 

**Still not working?**

If the steps above didn't help, try these next, in this order.

**Restart the phone**

Press and hold the side button and either volume button until the slider appears, drag it, then turn the phone back on. Restarting clears minor glitches.

**Reset network settings**

Go to **Settings** > **General** > **Transfer or Reset iPhone** > **Reset** > **Reset Network Settings**. This clears saved Wi-Fi networks and passwords, Bluetooth pairings and VPN settings, so get the customer's OK before they start.

On iPhone 8 and earlier, press and hold the top button instead of the side button to restart.

* * *

**Check the fix:** Have the customer turn on Airplane mode with Wi-Fi on, then make a test call. A step can look like it worked before it really has.

If none of this helps, connect the customer with a specialist. Last reviewed 2026. Written for iOS 26. Related: Turn Airplane mode on or off, Reset network settings, Back up your phone.

=== KB-132: Troubleshoot Dropped Calls - iOS (In-Store) ===
# **Troubleshoot Dropped Calls - iOS**

When calls keep cutting out, the phone is usually losing its connection to the network for a moment. A weak signal, an old setting or a software glitch are the usual causes. For in-store technicians with diagnostic tools only. Don't use this article on a phone or chat call. Work through the sections below in order, and check the fix after each one.

* * *

## 

**Before you start**

Find out what the customer already tried, so you don't repeat it. If calls only drop at home and the customer uses Wi-Fi calling there, use **Troubleshoot Wi-Fi Calling** instead.

* * *

## 

**Turn Airplane mode on and off**

Open **Control Center** by swiping down from the top-right corner, tap the airplane icon, wait 10 seconds, then tap it again. This makes the phone reconnect to the network.

* * *

## 

**Restart the phone**

Press and hold the side button and either volume button until the slider appears, drag it, then turn the phone back on. Restarting clears minor glitches.

* * *

## 

**Still not working?**

If the steps above didn't help, try these next, in this order.

**Update the software**

Go to **Settings** > **General** > **Software Update** and install anything available.

**Reset network settings**

Go to **Settings** > **General** > **Transfer or Reset iPhone** > **Reset** > **Reset Network Settings**. This clears saved Wi-Fi networks and passwords, Bluetooth pairings and VPN settings, so get the customer's OK before they start.

On iPhone 8 and earlier, press and hold the top button instead of the side button to restart.

* * *

**Check the fix:** Have the customer make a test call and stay on it for two minutes. A step can look like it worked before it really has.

If none of this helps, connect the customer with a specialist. Last reviewed 2026. Written for iOS 26. Related: Turn Airplane mode on or off, Reset network settings, Back up your phone.

When calls keep cutting out, the phone is usually losing its connection to the network for a moment. A weak signal, an old setting or a software glitch are the usual causes. For in-store technicians with diagnostic tools only. Don't use this article on a phone or chat call. Work through the sections below in order, and check the fix after each one.

* * *

## 

**Before you start**

Find out what the customer already tried, so you don't repeat it. If calls only drop at home and the customer uses Wi-Fi calling there, use **Troubleshoot Wi-Fi Calling** instead.

* * *

## 

**Turn Airplane mode on and off**

Open **Control Center** by swiping down from the top-right corner, tap the airplane icon, wait 10 seconds, then tap it again. This makes the phone reconnect to the network.

* * *

## 

**Restart the phone**

Press and hold the side button and either volume button until the slider appears, drag it, then turn the phone back on. Restarting clears minor glitches.

* * *

## 

**Still not working?**

If the steps above didn't help, try these next, in this order.

**Update the software**

Go to **Settings** > **General** > **Software Update** and install anything available.

**Reset network settings**

Go to **Settings** > **General** > **Transfer or Reset iPhone** > **Reset** > **Reset Network Settings**. This clears saved Wi-Fi networks and passwords, Bluetooth pairings and VPN settings, so get the customer's OK before they start.

On iPhone 8 and earlier, press and hold the top button instead of the side button to restart.

* * *

**Check the fix:** Have the customer make a test call and stay on it for two minutes. A step can look like it worked before it really has.

If none of this helps, connect the customer with a specialist. Last reviewed 2026. Written for iOS 26. Related: Turn Airplane mode on or off, Reset network settings, Back up your phone.

=== KB-138: Troubleshoot Wi-Fi Calling - iOS (In-Store) ===
# **Troubleshoot Wi-Fi Calling - iOS**

Wi-Fi calling lets the phone make calls over Wi-Fi where the signal is weak. When it stops working, calls at home drop or won't connect. For in-store technicians with diagnostic tools only. Don't use this article on a phone or chat call. Work through the sections below in order, and check the fix after each one.

* * *

## 

**Before you start**

Find out what the customer already tried, so you don't repeat it. If calls drop everywhere, not just on Wi-Fi, use **Troubleshoot Dropped Calls** instead.

* * *

## 

**Turn on Wi-Fi calling**

Go to **Settings** > **Cellular** > **Wi-Fi Calling** and turn on **Wi-Fi Calling on This iPhone**. It can take a few minutes to activate. On some phones the menu is called **Mobile Service**.

* * *

## 

**Forget the network and join it again**

Go to **Settings** > **Wi-Fi**, tap the info icon next to the network, tap **Forget This Network**, then join it again with the password.

* * *

## 

**Still not working?**

If the steps above didn't help, try these next, in this order.

**Restart the phone**

Press and hold the side button and either volume button until the slider appears, drag it, then turn the phone back on. Restarting clears minor glitches.

**Reset network settings**

Go to **Settings** > **General** > **Transfer or Reset iPhone** > **Reset** > **Reset Network Settings**. This clears saved Wi-Fi networks and passwords, Bluetooth pairings and VPN settings, so get the customer's OK before they start.

On iPhone 8 and earlier, press and hold the top button instead of the side button to restart.

* * *

**Check the fix:** Have the customer turn on Airplane mode with Wi-Fi on, then make a test call. A step can look like it worked before it really has.

If none of this helps, connect the customer with a specialist. Last reviewed 2026. Written for iOS 26. Related: Turn Airplane mode on or off, Reset network settings, Back up your phone.

=== KB-141: Troubleshoot Wi-Fi Calling - Android (In-Store) ===
# **Troubleshoot Wi-Fi Calling - Android**

Wi-Fi calling lets the phone make calls over Wi-Fi where the signal is weak. When it stops working, calls at home drop or won't connect. For in-store technicians with diagnostic tools only. Don't use this article on a phone or chat call. Work through the sections below in order, and check the fix after each one.

* * *

## 

**Before you start**

Find out what the customer already tried, so you don't repeat it. If calls drop everywhere, not just on Wi-Fi, use **Troubleshoot Dropped Calls** instead.

* * *

## 

**Turn on Wi-Fi calling**

**Samsung Galaxy devices:** Open the **Phone** app, tap the three dots > **Settings**, and turn on **Wi-Fi calling**. **Other Android devices (Pixel):** Open the **Phone** app, tap the three dots > **Settings** > **Calls** > **Wi-Fi calling**, and turn it on.

* * *

## 

**Forget the network and join it again**

**Samsung Galaxy devices:** Go to **Settings** > **Connections** > **Wi-Fi**, tap the gear next to the network, tap **Forget**, then join it again. **Other Android devices (Pixel):** Go to **Settings** > **Network & internet** > **Internet**, tap the network, tap **Forget**, then join it again.

* * *

## 

**Still not working?**

If the steps above didn't help, try these next, in this order.

**Restart the phone**

**Samsung Galaxy devices:** Press and hold the **Side key**, tap **Power off** > **Restart**. **Other Android devices (Pixel):** Press and hold the **Power** button, then tap **Restart**.

**Reset network settings**

**Samsung Galaxy devices:** Go to **Settings** > **General management** > **Reset** > **Reset network settings**. **Other Android devices (Pixel):** Go to **Settings** > **System** > **Reset options** > **Reset Wi-Fi, mobile & Bluetooth**. This clears saved Wi-Fi networks and passwords and Bluetooth pairings, so get the customer's OK before they start.

On older Samsung phones, **Data usage** may be under **Settings** > **Connections** > **Mobile networks**.

* * *

**Check the fix:** Have the customer turn on Airplane mode with Wi-Fi on, then make a test call. A step can look like it worked before it really has.

If none of this helps, connect the customer with a specialist. Last reviewed 2026. Written for Android 16. Related: Turn Airplane mode on or off, Reset network settings, Back up your phone.

**Turn Airplane mode on and off**

* * *

## 

**Restart the phone**

Press and hold the side button and either volume button until the slider appears, drag it, then turn the phone back on. Restarting clears minor glitches.

* * *

## 

**Still not working?**
